However, allowing machines to take over so many aspects of our lives can also lead to a regression in the overall social capabilities of humans. For example, many people will order food through an app or website, avoiding the social interaction associated with ordering food. While this is very convenient, it also leads to many people feeling anxious when ordering in person. ', '', '\tMy view is a combination of the utilitarian and dystopian views. I agree with the utilitarian view in that automation leads to a more progressive world, but that world also comes with drawbacks. The drawbacks are described in the dystopian view as losing part of our own humanity. While I think "losing part of our own humanity" is probably an extreme view of it, there is some truth to machines changing the way humans interact with one another.  ']
